questions.question: Valid Parentheses: which structure does the optimal O(n) solution rely on?
options: A queue, matching brackets in first-in first-out order
A stack holding the still-unmatched opening brackets
A HashMap counting how many of each bracket occur
A PriorityQueue ordered by bracket character
questions.explanation: Brackets must close in reverse order of opening, which is exactly LIFO; pure counting ignores order and would accept ([)].

questions.question: Number of Recent Calls: ping(t) counts pings in [t-3000, t]. Which structure is optimal?
options: A max-heap of every timestamp received
A monotonic decreasing stack of timestamps
A HashSet of the timestamps in the window
A queue, polling any timestamp older than t-3000
questions.explanation: Pings arrive in increasing time order, so the oldest is always the first to expire, which is exactly FIFO removal from the head of a queue.

questions.question: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation: why does this code pop into b before a?
options: The first pop returns the right operand, pushed most recently
ArrayDeque.pop() removes from the tail of the deque
Operands come back in the order they were pushed
Order is irrelevant because subtraction is commutative
questions.explanation: A stack returns the most recent push first, and in RPN that token is the right operand, which matters for the non-commutative - and / operators.

questions.question: Design Circular Queue: why keep a size counter (or one unused slot) besides head and tail?
options: To make enQueue run in O(1) instead of O(n)
To let the queue grow past its fixed capacity
head == tail cannot otherwise tell full from empty
Because % capacity is too slow to run on every call
questions.explanation: In a plain circular buffer the head and tail indices coincide both when the queue is empty and when it is full, so an extra size field disambiguates.

questions.question: Task Scheduler simulated step by step: which pair of structures models greedy scheduling with cooldown?
options: A min-heap of counts plus a HashSet of finished tasks
Two stacks, one for ready tasks and one for cooling
A stack of counts re-sorted after every time unit
A max-heap of counts plus a queue of cooling tasks
questions.explanation: The heap always hands back the task with the most runs left, and the FIFO queue releases each cooling task back to the heap exactly n intervals later.

questions.question: Valid Parentheses: what does this code do on the input ")"?
options: Returns false, because the empty stack pops nothing
Throws NoSuchElementException from pop()
Throws NullPointerException while unboxing null
Returns true, since the stack ends up empty
questions.explanation: ArrayDeque.pop() delegates to removeFirst(), which throws NoSuchElementException when empty; only peek() and poll() return null, so emptiness must be checked first.

questions.question: Implement Queue using Stacks: what is the cost of pop() in this two-stack design?
options: O(n) worst case and O(n) on average
O(log n) amortized per operation
O(1) amortized, O(n) for a call that transfers
O(1) worst case, since each stack op is O(1)
questions.explanation: Every element moves from in to out at most once, so n operations cost O(n) in total, even though the single pop that drains in is O(n).

questions.question: Implement Stack using Queues with a single queue: what does push(x) do right after offering x?
options: Reverses the queue with Collections.reverse
Polls and re-offers the other size-1 elements
Sorts the queue so the newest element leads
Swaps x with the head using an index-based set
questions.explanation: Rotating the older elements behind x leaves the newest at the head, so pop() and top() stay O(1) plain queue operations while push absorbs the O(n) cost.

questions.question: Daily Temperatures: what must the monotonic stack store, and why?
options: Temperatures, because the answer is a temperature gap
The running maximum temperature seen so far
Temperature-day pairs kept sorted in a PriorityQueue
Indices, so an answer is i minus the popped index
questions.explanation: The output is a number of days, a distance between positions, so the stack must hold indices; values alone cannot recover how far apart two days are.

questions.question: Next Greater Element II is circular. What is the standard way to handle the wrap-around?
options: Loop i from 0 to 2n-1 and index with i % n
Sort the array first, then run one monotonic pass
Reverse the array and sweep the stack once
Append the array maximum as an extra last element
questions.explanation: A second sweep over the same n values lets late elements see earlier ones, and anything still on the stack after 2n steps genuinely has no greater element.

questions.question: Asteroid Collision: when does the current asteroid actually collide with the stack top?
options: Whenever the two asteroids have different signs
Only when the top is negative and the current positive
Only when the top is positive and the current negative
Whenever the current one is larger in absolute value
questions.explanation: A positive asteroid on the stack moves right and a later negative one moves left, so only that arrangement closes the gap; a negative top has already flown away.

questions.question: Simplify Path: what should the code do when a token from the split is ".."?
options: Push ".." so the final join can resolve it
Pop one directory, doing nothing if empty
Clear the whole stack back down to the root
Pop two directories, one per dot character
questions.explanation: A ".." moves up exactly one level, and the root has no parent, so popping an empty stack must be a silent no-op rather than an error.

questions.question: Decode String, e.g. 3[a2[c]]: what does the iterative solution push when it reads '['?
options: Only the repeat count; the prefix is rebuilt later
The raw substring inside the brackets, unparsed
The index of the matching ']' found by pre-scanning
The repeat count and the string built so far
questions.explanation: Two stacks are needed, one for multipliers and one for the prefix before the bracket, so ']' can pop both and append count copies of the decoded inner string.

questions.question: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String: what is this StringBuilder-as-stack version's cost?
options: O(n^2), since deleteCharAt shifts the whole buffer
O(n log n), dominated by buffer growth
O(n), each char is appended once and removed at most once
O(n) only when the input has no adjacent duplicates
questions.explanation: Deleting the final character shifts nothing, so both branches are O(1) and every character enters and leaves the buffer at most once.

questions.question: Sliding Window Maximum: what invariant does the ArrayDeque maintain?
options: Values sorted ascending, so the tail holds the maximum
Every value in the window, rescanned for the maximum
Indices whose values decrease from front to back
Indices ordered by value, with the minimum at the front
questions.explanation: Holding indices in decreasing value order keeps the window maximum at the front, and storing positions lets expired indices be dropped in O(1) each.

questions.question: Largest Rectangle in Histogram: why is the width i - st.peek() - 1 after the pop?
options: It counts the bars strictly between the shorter left and right bars
It subtracts one because the popped bar is excluded
It is an off-by-one guard for a sentinel zero bar
It converts a 1-based index into a 0-based index
questions.explanation: After the pop, st.peek() is the nearest shorter bar on the left and i is the nearest shorter bar on the right, so the rectangle spans the open interval between them.

questions.question: Trapping Rain Water with a monotonic decreasing stack: what does one pop compute?
options: All the water sitting above that bar for the whole array
One horizontal slab bounded by the left and right taller bars
The vertical column of water resting on that single index
The prefix maximum height up to that index
questions.explanation: The popped bar is the floor and its new neighbours are the walls, so the slab is min(left,right) minus the floor high and as wide as the gap; two pointers sum columns instead.

questions.question: Sliding Window Maximum: what is wrong with the eviction test in this loop?
options: pollFirst should be pollLast, since a deque is FIFO
It must be <=, index i - k is already out of the window
The if must be a while, many indices can expire at once
offerLast must run before the trimming while loop
questions.explanation: The window is [i-k+1, i], so index i-k is stale; with a strict < it survives an extra step and can be reported as the maximum. Only one index can expire per step.

questions.question: Basic Calculator with + - and parentheses: what goes on the stack when '(' is read?
options: The characters inside the group, to be parsed later
The index of the matching ')' from a pre-scan
Only the sign, since the total can be recomputed
The result so far and the sign in front of the group
questions.explanation: Evaluation restarts inside the parentheses, so the outer partial sum and the sign multiplying the group must both be saved and restored when ')' arrives.

questions.question: Remove K Digits: which monotonic invariant makes this greedy loop yield the smallest number?
options: Keep digits non-decreasing: drop a digit bigger than the next
Keep digits non-increasing: drop a digit smaller than the next
Any order works as long as exactly k digits are removed
Delete the k largest digits, wherever they sit
questions.explanation: Removing a digit that exceeds its successor lowers the most significant differing place, so the surviving prefix is non-decreasing and minimal.

questions.question: Online Stock Span: what does the stack hold so that next(price) is amortized O(1)?
options: Every past price, rescanned backwards on each call
Only the maximum price so far plus a counter
Price-span pairs, whose spans merge when popped
A max-heap of prices popped while below today's
questions.explanation: Popping a smaller price folds its already computed span into today's span, so each price is pushed and popped at most once across all calls.

questions.question: Min Stack: which call sequence makes this pair of stacks report a wrong getMin()?
options: push(2), push(2), pop(), getMin()
push(1), push(2), pop(), getMin()
push(-1), push(0), getMin()
push(3), pop(), push(3), getMin()
questions.explanation: Strict < skips the duplicate minimum, then the equality check pops its only copy, so getMin() breaks while a 2 is still on the main stack; use <= on push.
